display.purpose: One page heading per screen (Home greeting, Projects, project overview).

headline.purpose: Project frame titles and the chat channel heading.

title.purpose: Section headings; modal titles 18px, module card titles 15px, compact headings 14px.

body-secondary.purpose: Descriptions and supporting copy in Print Grey; hero copy capped at 640px.

label.purpose: Sidebar group labels, column-block headings, form labels; sentence case, never tracked.

data.purpose: Task codes, counts, percentages, deadlines, kbd and status pills; tabular figures.

data-figure.purpose: The percentage under a test strip.

edge-print.purpose: Uppercase mono edge row on project frames (code and counts) in exposure-3; the only uppercase-tracked style, data only.

shadows.name: menu-drop
shadows.purpose: Account menu; board property menus use 0 16px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.45).

shadows.name: dialog-drop
shadows.purpose: Modals; auth card uses the same drop at 0.5.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Input focus, paired with a safelight border.

shadows.name: active-marker
shadows.purpose: Active nav item left edge; a mark, not depth.

motion.name: ease-develop
motion.purpose: The one entrance curve: strip bands, route entry, modals, voice dock.

motion.name: develop-band
motion.value: 640ms ease-develop, stagger 55ms per band; opacity 0 + brightness(.35) to 1
motion.purpose: Test strip bands developing in turn.

motion.name: modal-in
motion.purpose: Modal card rise; scrim fades in 180ms ease.

motion.name: hover
motion.value: 140ms ease (160ms on frames and room rows)
motion.purpose: Background, border and color state changes.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: Live voice lamps and live tags only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce cuts animation and transition durations to .01ms
motion.purpose: Every animation is cut under reduced motion.

components.name: Test Strip
components.description: Signature progress: ten bands lit from exposure-1 to full safelight, developing in turn; green when complete.

components.css: .ds-rooms { width: 312px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e241d); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--surface-1, #18120e); overflow: hidden; font-family: var(--font-ui, Geist, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-room { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 10px; align-items: center; padding: 10px 12px 10px 14px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border, #2e241d); color: var(--text, #ece0cf); transition: background 160ms ease; } .ds-room:first-child { border-top: 0; } .ds-room:hover { background: var(--surface-2, #211913); } .ds-room div { display: grid; gap: 1px; } .ds-room strong { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-room small { color: var(--muted, #968676); font-size: 12px; } .ds-room__lamp { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--seam-strong, #3d3027); } .ds-room__action { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid var(--seam-strong, #3d3027); border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: var(--text, #ece0cf); font: 600 12px var(--font-ui, Geist, system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; } .ds-room__action:hover { background: var(--surface-3, #2a211a); } .ds-room__action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--safe, #f07a1a); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-room--live { background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(240, 122, 26, 0.16), rgba(240, 122, 26, 0.03)); } .ds-room--live .ds-room__lamp { background: var(--safe, #f07a1a); animation: ds-pulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-room--live small { color: var(--safe-text, #f7a35c); } .ds-room__action--leave { border-color: rgba(240, 122, 26, 0.42); color: var(--safe-text, #f7a35c); } @keyframes ds-pulse { 50% { opacity: .35; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-room--live .ds-room__lamp { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
DaiHub is a darkroom. The room is warm black, work lies in trays one step lighter, text is print white, and a single daidai-orange safelight is the only lamp in the room. The safelight is not decoration: it marks what is live right now, such as the primary action, the page you are on, the voice room you are in, or the card you have selected. Everything else stays in the dark, and that restraint is what lets a founder read the room at a glance.

Progress is drawn as a darkroom test strip: ten stepped exposure bands that come up from deep amber to full safelight as a project or module develops, and turn green when the print is finished. The strip is the system's signature and its one motion idea. Bands develop one after another with a single slow fade-up, and the same develop curve carries route entry, modals and the voice dock.

The room is dense but quiet. It is built for a startup team at desktop monitors all day: a 232px rail, a 56px top bar, a main column of frames and a 312px side column for rooms and attention. Surfaces are separated by 1px warm seams rather than shadows. The world rejects the category default of navy-black panels with a violet or blue accent and glowing glass cards.
keyCharacteristics: Warm black room with three tray tones and 1px warm seams; no glass, no blur.
One safelight orange, reserved for what is live.
Geist for the interface; JetBrains Mono only for data (codes, counts, percentages, times).
Progress as a 10-band test strip, lighting from exposure-1 to full safelight and turning green when complete.
Small radii (4 to 8px) on everything in the page; 12px only on floating overlays.
One motion curve (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`), and every animation is cut under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Safelight Rule
rules.body: Full orange appears only on what is live: the primary action, the active location, the room you are connected to, the current selection and the focus ring. If nothing on a screen is live, the only orange on it is the primary button.

rules.name: The Three-Value Rule
rules.body: Room, tray and print carry the whole interface. Green, red and amber may enter only to report a state (done, danger or late, near or review).

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono sets only machine facts: codes, counts, percentages, times and shortcuts. Prose, labels and buttons stay in Geist.

rules.name: The Seam-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Anything that sits in the page is separated by a 1px seam and a tray step. A shadow means the element is floating above the page.

dos: **Do** keep full safelight (#f07a1a) for what is live: the primary action, the active location, the connected room, the current selection and focus.
**Do** separate in-page surfaces with a 1px seam and one tray step, and save shadows for floating overlays.
**Do** draw project and module progress as the 10-band test strip at lg, md or sm, never as a ring, and let it turn developed green only at 100%.
**Do** set codes, counts, percentages and times in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures; everything else is Geist.
**Do** use the authored 1.75-stroke icon set at 14 to 16px, and map stored module glyphs through it.
**Do** keep destructive actions outlined and neutral until hovered or focused, placed apart from status, with the filled red button only inside the confirm step.
**Do** animate entrances with the develop curve (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`), and keep hover transitions at 140 to 160ms.
donts: **Don't** introduce navy-black panels, a violet or blue accent, or glowing glass cards; that is the category default this world rejects.
**Don't** use glass, backdrop blur or colored glow halos on any surface.
**Don't** add a second accent hue; green, red and amber appear only as state.
**Don't** use radii above 8px on in-page surfaces, or pill shapes on buttons.
**Don't** render emoji or text characters as interface icons.
**Don't** set uppercase tracked labels above headings; the edge-print row is the only uppercase style, and it carries data.
